_doc: Batch m03 (medium, opus themed pass): ghost-slug, giant-banded-snail, herring-gull, tern-squadron, skua-raider, cormorant-line, booby-colony, turkey-vulture, mountain-buzzard, burrowing-owl, snowy-owl-scout. Every piece (unique and class) has a hand note. New motifs (24, all 11 signatures unique) are drawn by claude/pf-anim/motifs/medium_m03.js; one composition motif (guano-splat) is defined below. Shared secondaries on purpose: plunge-splash (tern, cormorant, booby: all plunge divers), hook-jab (skua, turkey-vulture, mountain-buzzard: hooked bills), thermal-spiral (turkey-vulture, mountain-buzzard: thermal soarers), talon-grip (buzzard, snowy owl), stolen-fish (skua, cormorant). Reused catalogue motifs: glass-glint (ghost-slug b2, see-through glimmer), croak-ring (snowy-owl u1, hoot rings), bunting-flurry (snowy-owl u2, white feathers in snow).

guano-splat.desc: white guano splats slapped down and sticking, crusting into a rough rim with dark flecks

ghost-slug.notes: Ghost slug: a pale see-through cave slug with a faint glow inside; it fades in and out and breathes cold cave air.

u0.n: Glow Ooze: see-through slugs rise off the edge, their glow cores brightening, a dotted afterglow behind

u1.n: Pale Sheen: the pale slugs slip out and back, fading half away, white sheen flecks where they were

u2.n: Cold Lunge: one ghost slug lunges along the whole edge in a cold haze

u3.n: Drift Veil: a veil of cold breath curls up and drifts out and back

b0.n: Cold Puddle Lunge: slugs lunge out of a cold puddle, drops flicked off

b1.n: Cave Mouth Chill: cold cave breath curls off the edge, frost specks at the tips

b2.n: Glimmer Shroud: hollow glassy outlines line the edge, a glint crossing them

b3.n: Puddle Shapeshift: the slug melts to a puddle and re-forms at spot after spot

giant-banded-snail.notes: Giant banded snail: a huge glossy yellow-brown shell with a dark spiral band, rolling slowly through rainforest leaf litter on a slimy foot.

u0.n: Banded Slam: the big banded shell slams out and drops back, dust thrown up

u1.n: Shell Spiral: shells roll out and back, the gloss highlight turning

u2.n: Slime Sheet: glossy slime films hang at spots, tied together by sticky strings

u3.n: Striped Roll: one banded shell rolls the length of the edge on a wet trail

b0.n: Leaf Litter Gnaw: shells lunge in, chewed leaf crumbs left behind

b1.n: Barrel-Shell Crush: the barrel shell crashes down hard

b2.n: Striped Barrel Hide: shells sit tight along the edge, the snail pulled in

b3.n: Litter Roll Over: slime and leaf litter flip at spot after spot

herring-gull.notes: Herring gull: a big white seaside gull with grey wings, black wingtips and a yellow bill with a red spot; a loud chip thief that raids the bins.

u0.n: Chip Thief: stolen hot chips dangle at spots, tied together, crumbs dropping

u1.n: Gull Swoop: a gull swoops the length of the edge, down and up

u2.n: Screech: gull heads throw back and screech, the wedges spreading out

u3.n: Bin Lid Clang: bin lids slam down and clang, clang marks flying

b0.n: Scrap-Snatch Peck: chips are snatched off the edge and tumble away

b1.n: Screaming Swoop: gulls swoop off the edge, angry marks above

b2.n: Gull-Wide Spread: gulls hang along the edge, grey wings spread wide

b3.n: Thief's Flap Away: the gulls flap off and back, crumbs falling from their bills

tern-squadron.notes: Tern squadron: slim white terns with black caps, red bills and long forked tails, flying in formation and plunging for fish.

u0.n: Dive Strike: the squadron streaks along the edge in a V, a spray jet where it hits

u1.n: Wing Wheel: the terns wheel out and back on a dotted arc

u2.n: Fish Snatch: terns fold and plunge, crown splashes jump up and fall

u3.n: Fly Past Cut: terns cut past off the edge, sharp cut lines behind

b0.n: Head-Aimed Stab: a tight V darts down the edge, red bills first

b1.n: Flock Stoop Dive: the flock stoops off the edge, a splash for each

b2.n: Formation Wing Screen: terns hold a staggered line along the edge

b3.n: Annoyed Break Away: the formation breaks and terns flick between spots

skua-raider.notes: Skua raider: a heavy brown sea pirate with white wing flashes and a hooked bill; it chases other birds until they drop their catch.

u0.n: Skua Stoop: a heavy skua stoops down the edge, swerving hard

u1.n: Beak Jab: hooked bills jab out of the edge one after another and tear

u2.n: Skua Cover: skuas hang along the edge, white wing flashes held out

u3.n: Steal In Flight: stolen fish tumble out and back through the air, drops flung

b0.n: Robber's Hooked Beak: the hooked bill snaps out and tears

b1.n: Raised-Arm Stoop: skuas stoop off the edge with wings raised, angry marks

b2.n: Heavy Brown Wall: heavy brown birds stand shoulder to shoulder, dust at their feet

b3.n: Loot-Grab Flight: a fish is grabbed and flicks from spot to spot

cormorant-line.notes: Cormorant line: dark cormorants with snake necks, hooked bills and emerald eyes, lined up on a post holding their wings out to dry, then diving low in the water.

u0.n: Dive Spear: a snake neck spears along the edge underwater, bubbles rising

u1.n: Rapid Surface: necks pop up out of the water, drops flung off

u2.n: Wing Dry: the line shuffles out and back, wings held out, drips falling

u3.n: Surfaced Catch: caught fish hang at spots, tied to the bills by a line

b0.n: Post Spear Peck: necks strike off the edge from the water

b1.n: Fish Plunge: cormorants plunge in, crown splashes and rings

b2.n: Sun-Dried Wings: cormorants line the edge, wings hung out, drops running down

b3.n: Line Shuffle: the birds on the post swap places spot to spot

booby-colony.notes: Booby colony: white seabirds on bright blue feet, strutting and lifting each foot high, plunging for fish from the cliff and crusting the rocks with guano.

u0.n: Blue Foot Strut: boobies strut out and back, one blue foot high, then the other

u1.n: Plunge: white boobies slam into the water, a big crown splash

u2.n: Guano Cover: white guano splats crust the edge into a rough spiky rim

u3.n: Rude Stamp: a blue foot stamps down at spot after spot

b0.n: Whistle Peck: boobies lunge off the edge, blue feet flashing

b1.n: Stamping Dive: a run of splashes races along the edge

b2.n: Cliff Wall Wings: a guano-white cliff wall lines the edge

b3.n: Rude Interruption: boobies barge out and back, cross marks above

turkey-vulture.notes: Turkey vulture: dark wings with silver flight feathers held in a shallow V, teetering on the wind, a tiny bare red head; it rides thermals and hisses.

u0.n: Wobble Glide: teetering Vs glide out and back, rocking side to side

u1.n: Sway Off: the vulture sways away and turns up at another spot

u2.n: Beak Rip: a bare red head rips along the edge, the hooked bill tearing

u3.n: Thermal Shrug: heat columns stand along the edge, a vulture circling in each

b0.n: Red-Head Gouge: the bare red head jabs out and gouges

b1.n: Thermal Stoop: Vs tip off the edge out of a heat haze

b2.n: Spread Wing Shield: wide dark Vs hang along the edge, silver feathers showing

b3.n: Thermal Lift-Off: a thermal lifts the bird straight up off the edge

mountain-buzzard.notes: Mountain buzzard: a broad mottled-brown hawk on very wide rounded wings, circling the ridges in thermals, its shadow sweeping the ground.

u0.n: Thermal Drop: a broad buzzard drops along the edge on a dotted stoop line

u1.n: Talon Clutch: talons reach off the edge, open, close and clench

u2.n: Soar Shadow: the buzzard's cross-shaped shadow slams over the edge and away

u3.n: Ridge Circle: buzzards circle out and back over a heat haze

b0.n: Ridge Hook Peck: a hooked yellow-based bill jabs and tears

b1.n: Mountain Thermal Stoop: talons first off the edge, grit kicked up

b2.n: Broad Brown Wing: very wide mottled wings line the edge

b3.n: Ridgeline Glide Off: the buzzard slips into a thermal and out again

burrowing-owl.notes: Burrowing owl: a small sandy spotted owl on long legs with a round head, white brows and yellow eyes, bobbing at the mouth of its burrow.

u0.n: Ground Strike: a long-legged owl runs the length of the edge, prints behind

u1.n: Dust Spurt: burrow mouths burst out of the edge, dust spurting

u2.n: Burrow Mouth: burrow mouths line the edge, yellow eyes blinking inside

u3.n: Dawn Nod: the owl bobs its head at spot after spot

b0.n: Bobbing Beak: owls bob and peck off the edge

b1.n: Burrow Bob Strike: an owl springs out of the burrow and drops back, dust

b2.n: Burrow Wing Hood: owls stand guard along the edge, bobbing

b3.n: Hole-Hop Retreat: the owls duck into their holes and pop back out

snowy-owl-scout.notes: Snowy owl scout: a white black-flecked tundra owl with big yellow eyes, sitting dead still on the snow, then dropping silently on its prey.

u0.n: Snow Swoop: white feathered talons strike off the edge, snow thrown

u1.n: Frost Hoot: hoot rings pulse out and back, snow falling through them

u2.n: Feather Wall: white feathers settle along the edge in the snow

u3.n: Blank Perch: blank white faces slip out and back, staring

b0.n: Snow-Still Peck: a staring face lunges out of the snow

b1.n: Sudden Snow Strike: talons drop off the edge, snow puffs

b2.n: Snowdrift Wing Cloak: owl faces sit in a snowdrift along the edge, blinking

b3.n: Vanishing Lift-Off: the owl vanishes into the snow and stares back from another spot
